title: Torque queue — morning checklist & quicknotes
content:
Morning run (personal) — quick checklist and scratchpad for torque/gpu queue ops

Goal: get an accurate snapshot and handle any obvious hotspots before standup. Keep notes short, actions visible.

Snapshot commands (fast):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide -l pool=gpu-inference   # look for NotReady/drain
- kubectl top pod -n inference | sort -nr -k3 | head 12  # top CPU consumers (scan for runaway jobs)
- kubectl top pod -n inference | grep -E '0m|0Mi'  # suspicious low metrics (evicted/gone)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-snap.csv & sleep 2; pkill -f "nvidia-smi -l"  # quick snapshot file
- qstat -u redwood  # legacy queue check, if still used by any legacy batch jobs

Quick checks / thresholds to scan for:
- Queue length > 80 pending for > 10m -> escalate (page on-call, mark capacity-plan)
- Average GPU utilization across pool < 20% but queue > 30 -> investigate scheduling/taints
- Memory errors (CUDA OOM) seen in pod logs -> add to node-drain candidate list
- Node flaps (NotReady -> Ready multiple times in last 30m): mark for investigation (networks + NIC firmware)

Immediate actions (if seen):
- If pod OOMs repeat on same node: cordon node; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node> 
  + leave note in node-tickets channel + create INF ticket with logs
- If autoscaler is saturated (desired > current by 2x for 15m): bump burst limit in console for dedicated pool and notify SREs
- If prefix cache miss spike: check redis metrics (prefix-cache-ops, hit_rate). If hit_rate < 0.6, temporarily increase cache size for 2h and measure

Notes to self (informal):
- Today: ~5 dev clusters running heavy reranking experiments (rp: rerank-ml). Watch latency tail.
- Spot reclaim pattern: aws-us-west-2b reclaim spikes at 03:10 UTC; correlate with our infra reclaim logs (last 3 days)
- Reminder: run small sim of the new batching heuristic against sampled trace (trace-runner/2026-03-08.json) before rolling out

Mini capacity table (rough):
- Pool: gpu-inference-a: 24 GPUs, avg util 72%, free ~6 GPUs
- Pool: gpu-inference-b: 40 GPUs, avg util 55%, free ~18 GPUs (buffer ok)
- Pool: gpu-burst: 8 GPUs, reserved for bursts, currently 0/8 used

Short todos (today):
- [ ] sanity-run quick watch for 30m after deploy to ensure KV cache warmup works (est 45m)
- [x] follow-up with Diego on INF-4821 autoscaler patch (left comments)
- [ ] add a logging filter for "cuMemcpy" OOM messages in Elasticsearch (me)
- [ ] update the small-runbook for transplanting jobs across taints (PR: github:repo/patches/183)

Deferred / backlog ideas (brainstorm):
- automatic preemptible backfill that prefers lower latency zones (cheap wins)
- node-level telemetry that tags first-failed-container to speed RCA (proto exists)
- a small web GUI to visualize per-customer token cost vs GPU usage for the burst pool

Open questions / unresolved:
- Does the new network firmware on the r730s improve NIC drop counts? Need lab test channel with SRE.
- Can we safely reduce prefix cache TTL to 30s for rerank workloads? risk: more misses during ramp. Plan: A/B during low traffic window.

Incident notes (if something went wrong last 24h):
- 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC: brief spike in latency (tail), traced to 2/40 nodes transient NIC drops. Temporary mitigations: route around AZ and drain effected nodes.
- Added ticket INF-4909 to track firmware QA and longer-term mitigation.

Useful links for this session:
- confluence: infra/gpu-operations (quick links)
- jira: INF-4821 (autoscaler patch)
- slack: #infra-gpu (pinned: runbook, night-ops)

Tiny heuristics (for me to remember):
- If 3+ nodes in AZ show >5% packet errors, assume fabric/ToR issue, escalate network team rather than draining nodes.
- Bump burst cap by +2 GPUs instead of +8 if unknown cause; conservative first.
